claim: Democracy requires free and fair elections an independent judiciary freedom of the press and protection of minority rights
Separation of powers divides government authority among legislative executive and judicial branches to prevent concentration of power
Federalism distributes power between a central government and regional or state governments
Proportional representation allocates legislative seats based on the percentage of votes each party receives
The United Nations has 193 member states and was founded in 1945 to maintain international peace and security
Gerrymandering manipulates electoral district boundaries to advantage particular parties or groups
The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 member states that operates through a hybrid system of supranational institutions
Direct democracy allows citizens to vote on policy directly rather than through elected representatives
Regulatory capture occurs when regulatory agencies serve the interests of the industries they are supposed to oversee
Freedom of information laws give citizens the right to access government documents and records
Ranked choice voting allows voters to rank candidates by preference eliminating the spoiler effect in multi-candidate elections
International humanitarian law including the Geneva Conventions protects persons who are not or are no longer participating in hostilities
The concept of sovereignty means that each state has supreme authority within its territory and is equal to other states in international law
Whistleblower protection laws shield individuals who report illegal or unethical activities within organizations from retaliation
Subsidiarity is the principle that decisions should be made at the most local level capable of addressing them effectively
